title: Legaltech Hub: Global Legal Technology Directory and News Briefs
answer: Legaltech Hub is a global directory of legal technology solutions, tools and services. It is aimed at buyers researching legal tech for law firms or in house departments, vendors showcasing solutions, and investors understanding the marketplace. The most useful thing it offers is a map of what exists before evaluating what works. The supplied text also includes short news items on AI moves by Relativity, NetDocuments, OpenAI, Steno and MiAI Law, but it remains mainly a directory landing page rather than a detailed report.

sections.body: Legaltech Hub publishes this page. It is a landing page for a global directory of legal technology solutions, tools and services. sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page presents Legaltech Hub as a global directory of legal technology solutions, tools and services. It says buyers can research legal tech to manage a 21st century law firm or in house department, vendors can showcase solutions, and investors can understand the marketplace. The supplied text then gives short news items. It reports that, ahead of RelFest 2026 in Chicago, Relativity announced AI moves: rebranding RelativityOne to Relativity aiR in September, launching Relativity claiR in August, acquiring document automation company Gavel in June, and releasing an MCP Connector to Claude or Legal in May. It says NetDocuments is building its AI strategy around the Legal Context Graph it launched in May, and with a new benchmark and two AI features argues that as models and legal tools become more interchangeable, the advantage shifts to firms that connect AI to their own documents, knowledge and legal authorities. It notes OpenAI released Astra for Law, built initially for Am Law 200 firms, described not as a new model but a model configuration pairing OpenAI's most recent GPT-6 Astra model with specific knowledge, tools and ecosystem plugins tailored for legal. It describes Transcript Genius as a Steno deposition transcript analysis tool using AI to mine deposition and trial transcripts for summaries, data points and strategic insights, and MiAI Law as an Australian legal AI platform combining case law research, legislative research, case summarization, contract review, and document and pleading verification.

sections.body: The source states that Legaltech Hub is a global directory of legal technology solutions, tools and services. sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in Legal can use this source as a starting map of the vendor landscape and as a short signal of recent AI moves. The directory framing helps identify categories and players, while the news items point to areas where AI is being applied, such as legal data intelligence, document automation, document and knowledge management, model configurations for law firms, deposition transcript analysis, and Australian legal research and contract review. It is most useful for orientation and discovery before evaluating what works, because it catalogues tools and vendors rather than testing them. The text does not compare product quality, outcomes or suitability for a particular firm or in house team.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Legal

sections.body: This is a landing page with little substantive detail. It does not provide methodology, selection criteria, pricing, rankings, independent evaluations or full article content. The news items are brief, some dates are month only, and the supplied text was harvested on 2026-09-29, so it is a snapshot. It mentions interviews with James Ehlers and Laina Chan but does not include them. The page says vendors can showcase their solutions, which suggests a commercial or promotional dimension, but the text does not explain how listings are selected or updated.
